minutes.headline: Select Board leaned toward using the town's right of first refusal on 250 Howard Street while negotiating with buyers.
minutes.summary: The board heard the Open Space Committee chair explain why the town should consider buying a Chapter 61 parcel at 250 Howard Street, and heard from the prospective buyers. Most members favored pursuing the purchase or a negotiated access solution, and one member opposed spending on cost grounds. The board also ratified an ADA committee appointment, adopted an amended toll booth policy, and reviewed draft special town meeting articles and FY21 budget adjustments.

public_comment.topic: Proposed Lobsters for Lunenburg fundraiser for first responders, a drive-through lobster meal at TCP plus a raffle.
Prospective buyers of 250 Howard Street described their ties to town and plan to build a home.
Offered the town a strip along the back boundary for access as an alternative to buying the whole parcel.
Asked about negotiated access to Northwest Town Forest through the Aero Estates agreement.
Two Parks Commission vacancies, and whether the DPW director position has been advertised.

votes.motion: Ratify the town manager's appointment of Lori Ann Tessier to the ADA committee, term to expire June 30, 2023.
Accept the amended toll booth policy.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town received a state grant and invested its own money in the earlier acquisition.
A member described the 15-acre parcel as roughly fifty thousand dollars.
Rollback tax and conveyance tax would be paid to the town if the town does not exercise its right.
The town manager listed revenue and expenditure adjustments for the special town meeting.
The town will receive a 40R density bonus payment into general fund receipts.

budget_items.topic: Brownfields redevelopment funding for 925 Mass Ave
budget_items.what_was_said: Applications are open and close Friday; the town manager recommended applying.

decisions.decision: Board signaled overwhelming interest in exercising right of first refusal; buyers asked to work with the Open Space Committee ahead of the Sept 29 special town meeting warrant close.
Sign policy tabled to next week for review.
Town manager evaluation composite to be reviewed this week and voted next week.

what_happened.line: The Select Board signaled strong interest in using the town's right of first refusal on the Chapter 61 parcel at 250 Howard Street, with no formal vote taken.
The prospective buyers were asked to work with the Open Space Committee before the warrant closes for the Sept 29 special town meeting.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment to the ADA committee, term to June 30, 2023, by a 5-0 vote.
The board accepted an amended toll booth policy, and tabled the sign policy to next week for review.
The town manager listed FY21 revenue and expenditure adjustments for the special town meeting, and the board will vote next week on the town manager's evaluation.

why_it_matters: If the town buys the 250 Howard Street parcel, the cost would come from the town budget, mostly taxes, and a special town meeting vote would likely be needed to approve it.
The FY21 adjustments drafted for the special town meeting would change how this year's town budget is balanced.
